You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:
        
CREATE TABLE stadium (
    Stadium_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Location TEXT,
    Name TEXT,
    Capacity INT,
    Highest INT,
    Lowest INT,
    Average INT,
    UNIQUE (Stadium_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE singer (
    Singer_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Name TEXT,
    Country TEXT,
    Song_Name TEXT,
    Song_release_year TEXT,
    Age INT,
    Is_male bool,
    UNIQUE (Singer_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE concert (
    concert_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    concert_Name TEXT,
    Theme TEXT,
    Stadium_ID TEXT,
    Year TEXT,
    UNIQUE (concert_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Stadium_ID) REFERENCES stadium(Stadium_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE singer_in_concert (
    concert_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Singer_ID TEXT   PRIMARY KEY,
    PRIMARY KEY (concert_ID, Singer_ID),
    UNIQUE (concert_ID, Singer_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Singer_ID) REFERENCES singer(Singer_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (concert_ID) REFERENCES concert(concert_ID)
);

What do you mean by “big stadium analysis” (capacity only, or also highest/average attendance)?

Here are a few useful SQL queries you can run depending on what you want:

### 1) Biggest stadiums by capacity
```sql
SELECT Stadium_ID, Name, Location, Capacity
FROM stadium
ORDER BY Capacity DESC;
```

### 2) “Big” stadiums above a threshold (edit the number)
```sql
SELECT Stadium_ID, Name, Location, Capacity
FROM stadium
WHERE Capacity >= 50000
ORDER BY Capacity DESC;
```

### 3) Big stadiums that have hosted the most concerts
```sql
SELECT s.Stadium_ID, s.Name, s.Location, s.Capacity,
       COUNT(c.concert_ID) AS concert_count
FROM stadium s
LEFT JOIN concert c
  ON c.Stadium_ID = s.Stadium_ID
GROUP BY s.Stadium_ID, s.Name, s.Location, s.Capacity
ORDER BY concert_count DESC, s.Capacity DESC;
```

### 4) Big stadiums by average attendance (if `Average` is attendance)
```sql
SELECT Stadium_ID, Name, Location, Capacity, Highest, Lowest, Average
FROM stadium
ORDER BY Average DESC;
```

Tell me which metric you want (capacity vs Average/Highest), and if you want a specific cutoff (e.g., top 5, capacity > 60,000).
I want to focus on concerts in stadiums with high capacity.

```sql
-- Concerts held in high-capacity stadiums (set the cutoff)
SELECT
  c.concert_ID,
  c.concert_Name,
  c.Theme,
  c.Year,
  s.Stadium_ID,
  s.Name   AS stadium_name,
  s.Location,
  s.Capacity
FROM concert c
JOIN stadium s
  ON c.Stadium_ID = s.Stadium_ID
WHERE s.Capacity >= 50000
ORDER BY s.Capacity DESC, c.Year DESC, c.concert_Name;
```

If you want “high capacity” to mean the top N stadiums instead of a fixed cutoff, tell me N (e.g., top 10).
make sure to focus on concerts that actually happened in the stadium

To ensure you only include concerts that actually happened in a stadium (i.e., the concert row successfully matches a real stadium), use an `INNER JOIN` (not `LEFT JOIN`) between `concert` and `stadium`:

```sql
-- Concerts that actually took place in a real stadium, limited to high-capacity stadiums
SELECT
  c.concert_ID,
  c.concert_Name,
  c.Theme,
  c.Year,
  s.Stadium_ID,
  s.Name AS stadium_name,
  s.Location,
  s.Capacity
FROM concert AS c
JOIN stadium AS s
  ON CAST(c.Stadium_ID AS INT) = s.Stadium_ID
WHERE s.Capacity >= 50000
ORDER BY s.Capacity DESC, c.Year DESC, c.concert_Name;
```

Note: in your schema `concert.Stadium_ID` is `TEXT` while `stadium.Stadium_ID` is `INT`, so I cast it to `INT` to make the join reliable. If your DB doesn’t support `CAST(... AS INT)`, tell me which database you’re using (SQLite/MySQL/Postgres/etc.).
I want to focus on events that took place in the stadiums with the highest seating capacity.

```sql
-- Events (concerts) that took place in the stadium(s) with the maximum seating capacity
SELECT
  c.concert_ID,
  c.concert_Name,
  c.Theme,
  c.Year,
  s.Stadium_ID,
  s.Name AS stadium_name,
  s.Location,
  s.Capacity
FROM stadium s
JOIN concert c
  ON CAST(c.Stadium_ID AS INT) = s.Stadium_ID
WHERE s.Capacity = (SELECT MAX(Capacity) FROM stadium)
ORDER BY c.Year DESC, c.concert_Name;
```
